interface.name: noctalia_material_manager_v1
interface.description: A scene describes only its owning wl_surface. It never grants access to other clients, textures, screenshots, global theme settings, or lock content. The compositor may omit optical rendering during session lock and snapshots.

interface.name: noctalia_material_surface_v1
interface.description: At most one object may exist per wl_surface. set_scene replaces pending scene state; the last valid pending scene becomes current with wl_surface commit. An empty plane list clears effects. Destruction clears effects. Payload is the bounded little-endian v5 codec in scene_descriptor.h: at most 65536 bytes and 64 planes. All coordinates are logical surface coordinates. Per-plane affine transform, clipping, radii, continuous corner power (2 to 10), concave corner flags, material parameters, palette tint, opacity and semantic IDs are explicit. Foreground pixels are composited after the optical planes. Parent planes group ordinary controls. Explicit independent controls may publish nested optical planes; each carries its optional rounded paint mask. Rejected payloads leave current and pending state intact. Optical lens radius and mapping affect sampling only; painted radii, mask coverage and input geometry remain independently owned.

request.name: set_scene
request.description: Payload must not exceed 4080 bytes, including for version 1 clients.

request.name: set_scene_chunk
request.description: Each nonempty chunk has at most 3072 bytes. Total size is 1 to 65536. Offset zero starts or replaces the single upload for this object. Subsequent chunks must have the same serial and total size and exactly the next byte offset. Invalid chunks discard the upload and emit rejected, preserving valid pending/current state. Only a complete, valid descriptor replaces pending state. A surface commit discards any incomplete upload. set_scene also discards an incomplete upload. Surface destruction releases upload state. The descriptor format remains v5; interface version does not negotiate descriptor versions.
